rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companion’s speech is introduced with قال without a conjunction because it functions as the question-and-answer turn in the dialogue.
rows.anchor: حكي كلام صاحبه بفعل القول بدون عطف للدلالة على أنه واقع موقع المحاورة والمجاوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about disbelief expresses astonishment and censure, not a genuine inquiry, since the companion knew the other was a polytheist.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام في قوله : { أكفرت بالذي خلقك } مستعمل في التعجب والإنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here kufr means associating partners with God, including denial of resurrection; the relative clause invokes God’s creation to expose the addressee’s ignorance.
rows.anchor: فالمراد بالكفر هنا الإشراك الذي من جملة معتقداته إنكار البعث ، ولذلك عرف بطريق الموصولية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause argues that people acknowledge God created them, so no other being deserves worship.
rows.anchor: فإنهم يعترفون بأن الله هو الذي خلق الناس فما كان غير الله مستحقا للعبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge of the first creation should prevent denial of the second, as cited in 50:15 and 30:27; the wording therefore insinuates the addressee’s ignorance.
rows.anchor: ثم إن العلم بالخلق الأول من شأنه أن يصرف الإنسان عن إنكار الخلق الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From dust points to the food components extracted from earth that make up the drop of semen, with 36:36 cited in support.
rows.anchor: من تراب } إشارة إلى الأجزاء التي تتكون منها النطفة وهي أجزاء الأغذية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nutfah means a man’s fluid and derives from a root meaning to flow.
rows.anchor: والنطفة : ماء الرجل ، مشتقة من النطف وهو السيلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawwāka means he fashioned you proportionately in form and function.
rows.anchor: و سواك } عدل خلقك ، أي جعله متناسبا في الشكل والعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition min in from dust and then from a drop marks origin.
rows.anchor: و ( من ) في قوله : { من تراب ثم من نطفة } ابتدائية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ten canonical readers pronounce the written alif in lakinnā when pausing; most omit it in connection, while Ibn ʿĀmir, Abū Jaʿfar, and Ruways from Yaʿqūb pronounce it, both allowed by the rasm.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { لكنا هو الله ربي } كتب في المصحف بألف بعد النون . واتفق القراء العشرة على إثبات الألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lakinnā combines the adversative particle lakin with ana; al-Zajjāj explains that the hamza was dropped for ease without a regular morphological cause.
rows.anchor: ولفظ { لكنا } مركب من ( لكن ) بسكون النون الذي هو حرف استدراك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the hamza was not omitted by a morphological rule, it is not treated as present; its vowel moves to the silent nūn, and the resulting two moving nūns assimilate.
rows.anchor: أصله : لكن أنا ، فحذفت الهمزة تخفيفا كما قال الزجاج ، أي على غير قياس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects deriving the word from emphatic lakinna with an elongated fatḥa: that particle requires an accusative noun, and no suitable first-person pronoun fits here.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن تكون ( لكن ) المشددة النون المفتوحتها أشبعت فتحتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ana is the subject, and huwa Allāhu rabbī is a clause with a pronoun of the matter and its predicate; the confession means my state is that Allah is my Lord, unlike yours.
rows.anchor: فأنا ) مبتدأ ، وجملة { هو الله ربي } ضمير شأن وخبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adversative counters the preceding boast, especially if the men are brothers or close friends who might be assumed to share beliefs.
rows.anchor: وموقع الاستدراك مضادة ما بعد ( لكن ) لما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Four emphases affirm one God: two nominal clauses, the pronoun of the matter, restrictive definiteness in Allah is my Lord, and the repeated denial of shirk.
rows.anchor: وأكد إثبات اعترافه بالخالق الواحد بمؤكدات أربعة ، وهي : الجملتان الاسميتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Walawlā is conjoined to the earlier denial as another censure; before entering the garden he should have said what God willed and that power belongs only to God, not boasted.
rows.anchor: وعطف جملة { ولولا إذ دخلت } على جملة { أكفرت } عطف إنكار على إنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation takes mā in mā shāʾ Allāh as a relative pronoun: this garden is what God willed to give me.
rows.anchor: و ( ما ) من قوله : ما شاء الله } أحسن ما قالوا فيها إنها موصولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers mā as an indefinite noun qualified by the following clause: this is something God willed for me.
rows.anchor: وأحسن منه عندي : أن تكون ( ما ) نكرة موصوفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No power belongs to the speaker to make the garden; human capacities are gifts from God and operate only with His help through sound means and tools.
rows.anchor: وجملة { لا قوة إلا بالله } تعليل لكون تلك الجنة من مشيئة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general statement that there is no power except through God explains why the garden is one instance of creation enabled by God-given human powers.
rows.anchor: فما في جملة { لا قوة إلا بالله } من العموم جعلها كالعلة والدليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reply answers the boast of greater wealth and supporters in 18:34: fortunes can shrink or disappear, while a poor person can become wealthy.
rows.anchor: رجع بها إلى مجاوبة صاحبه عن قوله : { أنا أكثر منك مالا وأعز نفرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker’s yāʾ is omitted after the protective nūn for ease, a common usage.
rows.anchor: وحذفت ياء المتكلم بعد نون الوقاية تخفيفا وهو كثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ana is a separating pronoun, so aqalla is accusative as the second object of tara.
rows.anchor: و ( أنا ) ضمير فصل ، فلذلك كان أقل } منصوبا على أنه مفعول ثانن ل { ترن }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAsā expresses hope in something near at hand and may be a prayer for the speaker and his companion.
rows.anchor: و ( عسى ) للرجاء ، وهو طلب الأمر القريب الحصول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥusbānan is like ghufrān and here describes an omitted noun, a divinely measured destruction.
rows.anchor: والحسبان : مصدر حسب كالغفران . وهو هنا صفة لموصوف محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations of ḥusbān are a volley of short arrows, a collective noun for lightning, or locusts; all four senses suit the context.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الحسبان اسم جمع لسهام قصار يرمى بها في طلق واحد وليس له مفرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky here means the elevated atmosphere above the earth.
rows.anchor: والسماء : الجو المرتفع فوق الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣaʿīd means the earth’s surface, as in 5:6; this prepares for describing it as slippery.
rows.anchor: والصعيد : وجه الأرض . وتقدم عند قوله تعالى : فتيمموا صعيدا طيبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Layth reportedly used ṣaʿīd for a ruined garden made level and treeless; if authentic, this suits the verse’s emphasis on complete uselessness.
rows.anchor: وفي ( اللسان ) عن الليث ( يقال للحديقة ، إذا خربت وذهب شجراؤها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr suspects al-Layth inferred that sense from this verse rather than recording the word’s established meaning; 18:8 offers a parallel expression.
rows.anchor: لكني أظن أن الليث ابتكر هذا المعنى من هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zalaq is a verbal noun for slipping and instability; describing the land as slippery intensifies its complete lack of benefit.
rows.anchor: والزلق : مصدر زلقت الرجل ، إذا اضطربت وزلت على الأرض فلم تستقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plants’ intermingling means abundant growth with its parts entwined through fertility and flourishing.
rows.anchor: واختلاط النبات : وفرته والتفاف بعضه ببعض من قوة الخصب والازدهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ is causal and its pronoun refers to water: plants mingle because of the water; it does not make ikhtalaṭ transitive.
rows.anchor: والباء في قوله : ( به ) باء السببية . والضمير عائد إلى ( ماء )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning earth after sky creates antithesis.
rows.anchor: وفي ذكر الأرض بعد ذكر السماء محسن الطباق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aṣbaḥa is used commonly to mean became.
rows.anchor: و ( أصبح ) مستعملة بمعنى صار ، وهو استعمال شائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hashīm follows faʿīl with passive meaning, crushed or shattered; hashm means breaking and fragmenting.
rows.anchor: والهشيم : اسم على وزن فعيل بمعنى مفعول ، أي مهشوما محطما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tadhruhu al-riyāḥ means winds scatter it through the air; dharw is throwing into the air.
rows.anchor: و { تذروه الرياح } أي تفرقه في الهواء . والذرو : الرمي في الهواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first simile compares worldly life to a garden whose beauty lasts, then declines; its shared feature is a turn from good to bad, an abstract condition pictured sensorially.
rows.anchor: شبهت حالة هذا العالم بما فيه بحالة الروضة تبقى زمانا بهجة خضرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second composite simile maps prosperity, youth, novelty, and adornment followed by contraction and scattered loss onto rain, abundant growth, decline, and windblown remnants.
rows.anchor: شبهت هيئة إقبال نعيم الدنيا في الحياة مع الشباب والجدة وزخرف العيش لأهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing clause is parenthetical: God’s power creates things and their opposites and orders causes of decay after causes of persistence; the universal wording serves as a conclusion.
rows.anchor: وجملة { وكان الله على كل شيء مقتدرا } جملة معترضة في آخر الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage answers those who worship useless idols as patrons and seek their favor, making their work and effort futile; the key rebuke is that they think they do well.
rows.anchor: فإنهم لما اتخذوا أولياء من ليسوا ينفعونهم فاختاروا الأصنام وعبدوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beginning with the command say signals an important utterance deserving attentive listening.
rows.anchor: وافتتاح الجملة بالأمر بالقول للاهتمام بالمقول بإصغاء السامعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question whether to inform them is an offer used ironically: the speaker will inform them regardless of their assent.
rows.anchor: وكذلك افتتاحه باستفهامهم عن إنبائهم استفهاما مستعملا في العرض لأنه بمعنى : أتحبون أن ننبئكم بالأخسرين أعمالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording shifts from direct address to third person, building curiosity before revealing that the losers are the listeners themselves.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله { بالأخسرين أعمالا } إلى آخره . . . تمليح إذ عدل فيه عن طريقة الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists are addressed to rebuke them and alert them to the failure of their efforts.
rows.anchor: والمقول لهم : المشركون ، توبيخا لهم وتنبيها على ما غفلوا عنه من خيبة سعيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural nūn in nunabbiʾukum may be God’s majestic plural, with narrative shift from expected he informs you.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن تكون نون العظمة راجعة إلى ذات الله على طريقة الالتفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the plural nūn may refer to the Messenger together with God, or to the Messenger and Muslims.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون راجعة للرسول وللمسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those whose effort went astray is an appositive to the losers, extending the description to heighten suspense about their identity.
rows.anchor: وقوله { الذين ضل سعيهم } بدل من { بالأخسرين أعمالا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍalāl means missing the path; unfruitful effort is likened to travel along a road that leads nowhere.
rows.anchor: والضلال : خطأ السبيل . شبه سعيهم غير المثمر بالسير في طريق غير موصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saʿy literally means vigorous walking and is metaphorical for work, as in 17:19; they worshiped idols believing their acts would fulfill their aims and count as good.
rows.anchor: والسعي : المشي في شدة . وهو هنا مجاز في العمل كما تقدم عند قوله { ومن أراد الآخرة وسعى لها سعيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing error to the effort is a figurative attribution: the people themselves went astray in their efforts.
rows.anchor: وإسناد الضلال إلى سعيهم مجاز عقلي . والمعنى : الذين ضلوا في سعيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaḥsabūn and yuḥsinūn form a paronomasia distinguished by dot placement, an example in the rhetoric manuals.
rows.anchor: وبين يحسبون } و { يحسنون } جناس مصحف ، وقد مثل بهما في مبحث الجناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ātī al-Raḥmān ʿabdan figuratively means acknowledging God and confessing His divinity; ʿabdan is a circumstantial accusative for a dependent servant.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { آتي الرحمن عبدا } : الإتيان المجازي ، وهو الإقرار والاعتراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes āti al-Raḥmān as coming to Him after death: one lives and is resurrected as a servant, never as a son.
rows.anchor: ويجوز جعل { آتي الرحمن } بمعنى صائر إليه بعد الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse contrasts believers’ affectionate fellowship at resurrection with the polytheists’ isolation in the previous verse.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية وصف لحال المؤمنين يوم القيامة بضد حال المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding isolation suggests condemned people wishing for a rescuer; believers instead receive affection and honor.
rows.anchor: أعقب ذلك بذكر حال المؤمنين الصالحين ، وأنهم على العكس من حال المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that the Merciful gives believers angelic friends and affection among themselves, as in 41:31 and 7:43.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى : سيجعل لهم الرحمن أوداء من الملائكة كما قال تعالى : { نحن أولياؤكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Choosing the verbal noun wudd allows it to cover several relations of affection.
rows.anchor: وإيثار المصدر ليفي بعدة متعلقات بالود

rows.speaker: قتيبة بن سعيد
rows.claim: A Tirmidhi report through al-Darāwardī explains that God places love for believers in the hearts of good people.
rows.anchor: رواه الترمذي عن قتيبة بن سعيد عن الدراوردي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr calls the report’s added wording a Qutaybah insertion unique to his Tirmidhi transmission.
rows.anchor: فهذه الزيادة إدراج من قتيبة عند الترمذي خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most apparent explanation is that God makes love for believers from Himself, as in 20:39; commentators offered other explanations of varying merit.
rows.anchor: هذا أظهر الوجوه في تفسير الود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra is named Ṭā Hā after its two opening letters, written in their muṣḥaf shapes rather than their spoken letter names, as in al-Aʿrāf.
rows.anchor: سميت سورة ( طاها ) باسم الحرفين المنطوق بهما في أولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name also appears in the Sunna account of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb’s conversion.
rows.anchor: وكذلك وردت تسميتها في كتب السنة في حديث إسلام عمر بن الخطاب

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report in al-Dārimī says God recited Ṭā Hā two thousand years before creating heaven and earth; angels rejoiced for the community to whom it would descend.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير القرطبي } عن ( مسند الدرامي ) عن أبي هريرة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن فورك
rows.claim: Ibn Fūrak interprets the report as God making His speech audible to whichever angels He wished to hear it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن فورك : معناه أن الله أظهر كلامه وأسمعه من أراد أن يسمعه من الملائكة

rows.speaker: السخاوي
rows.claim: Al-Sakhāwī says the sūra is also called Sūrat al-Kalīm.
rows.anchor: وذكر في ( الإتقان ) عن السخاوي أنها تسمى أيضا ( سورة الكليم )

rows.speaker: الهذلي
rows.claim: Al-Hudhali’s Complete names it Sūrat Mūsā.
rows.anchor: وفيه عن الهذلي في ( كامله ) أنها تسمى ( سورة موسى )

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority hold that the whole sūra is Meccan; Ibn ʿAṭiyya and many commentators state this.
rows.anchor: وهي مكية كلها على قول الجمهور

rows.speaker: السخاوي
rows.claim: Al-Itqān reports an exception for 20:130 and considers 20:131 another likely exception from the Meccan classification.
rows.anchor: وفي ( الإتقان ) أنه استثني منها آية : { فاصبر على ما يقولون وسبح بحمد ربك قبل طلوع الشمس

rows.speaker: أبو رافع
rows.claim: Abū Rāfiʿ reports that after a Jewish man refused to lend flour without collateral, the Prophet declared his trustworthiness and 20:131 was revealed.
rows.anchor: لما أخرج أبو يعلى والبزار عن أبي رافع قال : ( أضاف النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ضيفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Abū Rāfiʿ’s report is sound, Ibn ʿĀshūr thinks it confuses recitation with revelation: he may have heard the Prophet recite a familiar verse and assumed it had just descended.
rows.anchor: وعندي أنه إن صح حديث أبي رافع فهو من اشتباه التلاوة بالنزول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the report may use descent to mean recitation; such confusion recurs in transmitted occasions of revelation.
rows.anchor: أو أطلق النزول على التلاوة . ولهذا نظائر كثيرة في المرويات في أسباب النزول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lizāman denotes severe destruction, as in the cited poetic phrase; grammatically it is the predicate of kāna and refers to the annihilation implied by earlier mention of destroyed generations.
rows.anchor: أي : لكان الإهلاك الشديد لازما لهم . فانتصب { لزاما على أنه خبر ( كان )

rows.speaker: العرجي
rows.claim: The poem’s saddād witnesses the word for resoluteness or a firm defense at a difficult time.
rows.anchor: وسداد في قول العرجي : أضاعوني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fixed term is coordinated with the prior divine word: without both, annihilation would have been inevitable; the term may be worldly punishment such as Badr or punishment after death.
rows.anchor: { وأجل مسمى } عطف على { كلمة } والتقدير : ولولا كلمة وأجل مسمى يقع عنده الهلاك

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: A report in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī lists the smoke, moon, Romans, great assault, and lizām among five events already past, identifying the threatened punishment with Quraysh’s fate at Badr.
rows.anchor: ففي ( صحيح البخاري ) عن ابن مسعود قال : ( خمس قد مضين : الدخان ، والقمر ، والروم ، والبطشة ، واللزام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr says the Qurʾān does not require interpreting lizām as a punishment reserved for the end of the world.
rows.anchor: وليس في القرآن ما يحوج إلى تأويل اللزام بهذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to endure their denials and delayed threat, without hurrying the punishment; their words cover all such rejection.
rows.anchor: وفرع على ذلك أمر رسول الله بالصبر على ما يقولون من التكذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He should devote himself to purifying himself and his household through prayer, disregard the disbelievers’ worldly comforts, and trust that the God-fearing prevail.
rows.anchor: وأمره بأن يقبل على مزاولة تزكية نفسه وتزكية أهله بالصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbīḥ here means prayer because prayer includes glorifying and declaring God free of imperfection.
rows.anchor: فالتسبيح هنا مستعمل في الصلاة لاشتمالها على تسبيح الله وتنزيهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ in bi-ḥamdi rabbika marks accompaniment by the agent; the phrase functions circumstantially as praising the Lord while glorifying Him.
rows.anchor: والباء في قوله { بحمد ربك } للملابسة ، وهي ملابسة الفاعل لفعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The specified times are the prayers: dawn before sunrise; noon and afternoon before sunset, or afternoon alone; and from nightfall, sunset and night prayers, as clarified by mass-transmitted Sunna.
rows.anchor: والأوقات المذكورة هي أوقات الصلوات ، وهي وقت الصبح قبل طلوع الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take the two times before sunset as only the afternoon prayer, with noon included under the ends of the day.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد صلاة العصر . وأما الظهر فهي قوله : { وأطراف النهار } كما سيأتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min in min ānāʾ al-layl marks the starting point and attaches to fasabbiḥ.
rows.anchor: و { من } في قوله { من آناء الليل } ابتدائية متعلقة بفعل ( فسبح )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fronted time phrase receives emphasis, so fa is used as if the verb were a conditional response, as in the Prophetic command about both parents and in 17:79.
rows.anchor: وأدخلت الفاء على { فسبح } لأنه لما قدم عليه الجار والمجرور للاهتمام شابه تقديم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night hours receive special emphasis because people tend toward rest then and may neglect prayer.
rows.anchor: ووجه الاهتمام بآناء الليل أن الليل وقت تميل فيه النفوس إلى الدعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ānāʾ al-layl means its hours; Ibn ʿĀshūr lists singular forms in ini, inu, inā, and anāʾ, with plural ānāʾ on the afʿāl pattern.
rows.anchor: وآناء الليل : ساعاته . وهو جمع إني بكسر الهمزة وسكون النون وياء في آخره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa-aṭrāfa al-nahār is accusative, coordinated with before sunrise; ṭaraf is an endpoint.
rows.anchor: وقوله وأطراف النهار } بالنصب عطف على قوله { قبل طلوع الشمس }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation takes the ends as the beginning and end of day, dawn and sunset, with part singled out from the whole as in the emphasized middle prayer in 2:238.
rows.anchor: قيل : المراد أول النهار وآخره ، وهما وقتا الصبح والمغرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation means the sun’s arc endpoints, including its midpoint at noon; 11:114 uses the ends of the day, and the two endpoints can frame the time of one prayer.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المراد طرف سير الشمس في قوس الأفق ، وهو بلوغ سيرها وسط الأفق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This describes people neither secure in Islam nor wholly rejecting it: they enter while weighing the new faith against their former religion and watch what follows.
rows.anchor: هذا وصف فريق آخر من الذين يقابلون الأمر بالتقوى والإنذار بالساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If good follows conversion, they conclude Islam is true because their former gods failed to punish them; ordinary misfortune makes them resent Islam and return to old beliefs.
rows.anchor: فإن أصابهم الخير عقب ذلك علموا أن دينهم القديم ليس بحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On misfortune they imagine their former gods harmed them for abandoning worship, as the people of ʿĀd claimed in 11:54.
rows.anchor: سخطوا على الإسلام وانخلعوا عنه . وتوهموا أن آلهتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worshiping God on an edge means worshiping God alone, as the following verse’s contrast with calling on others shows.
rows.anchor: فالعبادة في قوله تعالى { من يعبد الله على حرف } مراد بها عبادة الله وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse apparently came down in Medina; Ibn ʿAbbās reports in Bukhārī that a migrant judged the faith good if his wife bore a son and his horse produced a foal, bad otherwise.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن هذه الآية نزلت بالمدينة ، ففي ( صحيح البخاري ) عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says it was revealed about hypocrites who had been polytheists, including ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية الحسن : أنها نزلت في المنافقين يعني المنافقين من الذين كانوا مشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr finds al-Ḥasan’s explanation unlikely because concealed unbelief does not fit people reassured when good follows conversion.
rows.anchor: وهذا بعيد لأن أولئك كانوا مبطنين الكفر فلا ينطبق عليهم قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ʿUrayniyyūn exemplify this group: after converting and migrating, they disliked Medina, recovered by drinking charity-camel milk and urine, then killed the shepherd, stole camels, and were captured and executed by the Prophet’s order.
rows.anchor: وممن يصلح مثالا لهذا الفريق العرنيون الذين أسلموا وهاجروا فاجتووا المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamz literally means pressure by hand or a jab with a finger, and figuratively means harm by speech or gesture, as in 68:11 and 104:1.
rows.anchor: والهمز حقيقته : الضغط باليد والطعن بالإصبع ونحوه ، ويستعمل مجازا بمعنى الأذى بالقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr takes the term figuratively under either interpretation of the devils.
rows.anchor: ومحمله هنا عندي على المعنى المجازي على كلا الوجهين في المراد من الشياطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jinn devils’ harm is clear; human devils harmed the Prophet through mockery, winking, and plotting.
rows.anchor: وأما همز شياطين الإنس فقد كان من أذى المشركين النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لمزه والتغامز عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking refuge means protection from the effects of their incitement, including goading a fool to harm the Prophet, as when someone threw a camel’s afterbirth on him during prayer at the Kaʿba.
rows.anchor: فإن من ذلك أن يغمزوا بعض سفهائهم إغراء لهم بأذاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This interpretation of the devils best suits the stated endpoint, when one of them meets death.
rows.anchor: وهذا الوجه في تفسير الشياطين هو الأليق بالغاية في قوله { حتى إذا جاء أحدهم الموت }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking refuge from the devils’ presence is protection from the harm their proximity brings.
rows.anchor: فهو تعوذ من قربهم لأنهم إذا اقتربوا منه لحقه أذاهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥattā is an independent transition, not an endpoint for the preceding statement and need not attach to “they describe”; it connects instead to God’s ability to show the threatened punishment in 23:95.
rows.anchor: والوجه أن ( حتى ) متصلة بقوله { وإنا على أن نريك ما نعدهم لقادرون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage shifts from worldly punishment to their afterlife punishment; if the earlier threats referred to the afterlife, they summarize what this passage details.
rows.anchor: فهذا انتقال إلى وصف ما يلقون من العذاب في الآخرة بعد أن ذكر عذابهم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronouns refer back to the polytheists who asked whether they would be resurrected after becoming dust and bones, not to the devils; the scene embeds a threat of punishment and regret.
rows.anchor: وضمائر الغيبة عائدة إلى ما عادت عليه الضمائر السابقة من قوله { قالوا أإذا متنا وكنا ترابا وعظاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural imperative irjiʿūn addresses one person honorifically, a recognized Arabic form that uses masculine plural even when honoring a woman.
rows.anchor: وضمير الجمع في { ارجعون } تعظيم للمخاطب . والخطاب بصيغة الجمع لقصد التعظيم طريقة عربية

rows.speaker: العرجي
rows.claim: Al-ʿArjī uses the plural suffix in siwākum when addressing one person honorifically.
rows.anchor: قال العرجي : فإن شئتت حرمت النساء سواكم

rows.speaker: جعفر بن علبة الحارثي
rows.claim: Jaʿfar ibn ʿUlba al-Ḥārithī likewise uses the honorific plural in baʿdakum.
rows.anchor: وقال جعفر بن علبة الحارثي من شعراء الحماسة : فلا تحسبي أني تخشعت بعدكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause of hope gives the reason for the request to be returned.
rows.anchor: وجملة الترجي في موضع العلة لمضمون { ارجعون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tark may retain its literal sense of leaving: what the speaker left behind is the world.
rows.anchor: والترك هنا مستعمل في حقيقته وهو معنى التخلية والمفارقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, figurative rejection means the faith in God and His messenger that the unbeliever refused; the plea promises obedience and admits past error.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد بالترك معناه المجازي وهو الإعراض والرفض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rebukes the listener and signals that the unbeliever’s request is invalid.
rows.anchor: و { كلا } ردع للسامع ليعلم إبطال طلبة الكافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause that it is merely a word is a Quranic, proverbial construction: the request is only speech and will not be answered.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { إنها كلمة هو قائلها } تركيب يجري مجرى المثل وهو من مبتكرات القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since it is obvious he says the word, the description means it has no quality beyond being uttered; inna emphasizes that point.
rows.anchor: وإذ كان من المحقق أنه قائلها لم يكن في وصف { كلمة } به فائدة جديدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalima means utterance, as in the Prophetic report quoting Labīd and in the formulas for the testimony and Islam; 9:74 uses it similarly.
rows.anchor: والكلمة هنا مستعمل في الكلام كقول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( أصدق كلمة قالها شاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Warāʾ is a metaphor for something inevitably approaching and reaching someone unaware, like a pursuer catching up; examples occur in 85:20, 45:10, 14:17, and 18:79.
rows.anchor: والوراء هنا مستعار للشيء الذي يصيب المرء لا محالة ويناله وهو لا يظنه يصيبه

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labīd’s verse uses warāʾ for what lies ahead as one’s death approaches.
rows.anchor: وقال لبيد : أليس ورائي أن تراخت منيتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Barzakh means a barrier between two places; reported interpretations are the grave, the remaining span of worldly life, or an intermediate realm where souls see their future station, favored by Sufis.
rows.anchor: والبرزخ : الحاجز بين مكانين . قيل : المراد به في هذه الآية القبر ، وقيل : هو بقاء مدة الدنيا

rows.speaker: السيد
rows.claim: Al-Sayyid’s Definitions calls barzakh the perceptible realm between abstract meanings and material bodies, or the imaginal world in ancient philosophy.
rows.anchor: وقال السيد في ( التعريفات ) : البرزخ العالم المشهود بين عالم المعاني المجردة وعالم الأجسام المادية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Until they are raised means the dead will not return to life before resurrection, extinguishing their hope because they know resurrection brings no return to worldly life.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { إلى يوم يبعثون } أنهم غير راجعين إلى الحياة إلى يوم البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trumpet clause branches from the resurrection deadline: instead of saying when resurrection comes, it paints the scene of the trumpet being blown.
rows.anchor: تفريع على قوله { إلى يوم يبعثون } ( المؤمنون : 100 ) فإن زمن النفخ في الصور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ṣūr is a horn blown for assembly or alarm, used for war and Jewish prayer; a Bukhārī report on the beginning of the call to prayer is cited, as is 6:73.
rows.anchor: والصور : البوق الذي ينفخ فيه النافخ للتجمع والنفير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive verb emphasizes the occurrence of the blowing rather than who blows; God commands it, or an angel such as Isrāfīl does so.
rows.anchor: وأسند { نفخ } إلى المجهول لأن المعتنى به هو حدوث النفخ لا تعيين النافخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The main consequence concerns the weighed deeds, answering the rejected plea for return; the denial of kinship first cuts off hope of help or intercession.
rows.anchor: والمقصود التفريع الثاني في قوله { فمن ثقلت موازينه } إلى آخره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most likely answer to when the trumpet is blown is the later question about how long they stayed on earth; intervening material is parenthetical.
rows.anchor: والأظهر أن جواب ( إذا ) هو قوله الآتي { قال كم لبثتم في الأرض عدد سنين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in baynahum refers to the preceding plural pronouns, namely the polytheists.
rows.anchor: وضمير { بينهم } عائد إلى ما عادت عليه ضمائر جمع الغائبين قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Denying kinship denies its customary benefits of support, rescue, and intercession, indirectly saying there is no helper.
rows.anchor: ومعنى نفي الأنساب نفي آثارها من النجدة والنصر والشفاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Questioning one another means asking for help during the terror, as in 70:10; the questioning in 37:27–33 occurs after they despair of any helper or intercessor.
rows.anchor: والتساؤل : سؤال بعضهم بعضا . والمعني به التساؤل المناسب لحلول يوم الهول

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In Bukhārī, Ibn ʿAbbās answers Nāfiʿ ibn al-Azraq that the denial of kinship and questioning is at the first trumpet, while mutual questioning is after the second.
rows.anchor: وفي ( البخاري ) : أن رجلا ( هو نافع بن الأزرق الخارجي ) قال لابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning heavy scales praises believers and threatens polytheists, who have no good deeds on their scales; 25:23 is cited and 7:8 is discussed earlier.
rows.anchor: وذكر من { ثقلت موازينه } في هذه الآية إدماج للتنويه بالمؤمنين وتهديد المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Loss originally describes failed trade; here it depicts ruined hopes for idol intercession or escape from resurrection, as in 6:12 and 7:9.
rows.anchor: والخسارة : نقصان مال التجارة وتقدم في قوله تعالى : { الذين خسروا أنفسهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They lose themselves because they expected salvation but found its opposite after rejecting Islam, as if their own selves had perished.
rows.anchor: وهي هنا تمثيل لحال خيبتهم فيما كانوا يأملونه من شفاعة أصنامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anfusahum is the direct object of khasirū, while the demonstratives distinguish the two groups by their qualities.
rows.anchor: ولذلك نصب { أنفسهم } على المفعول ب { خسروا } . واسما الإشارة لزيادة تمييز الفريقين

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read qāla in the past tense, placing the question after the trumpet and resurrection; it is most likely the answer to the earlier conditional in 23:101.
rows.anchor: قرأ الجمهور : { قال كم لبثتم } بصيغة الماضي فيتعين أن هذا القول يقع عند النفخ في الصور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects placing the question after unbelievers enter Hell as inconsistent with the discourse; the intervening verses are digressions.
rows.anchor: وليس من المناسب أن يكون هذا القول حاصلا بعد دخول الكافرين النار

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Ḥamzah, and al-Kisāʾī read qul as an imperative addressed to the angel tasked with reviving the dead.
rows.anchor: ابن كثير وحمزة و الكسائي { قل } بصيغة الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their referral to the counters follows from uncertainty about the duration; Ibn ʿĀshūr suggests they invoke their worldly difficulty calculating years because of the nasīʾ calendar managed by Banū Kināna.
rows.anchor: وأرى في تفسير ذلك أنهم جاءوا في كلامهم بما كان معتادهم في حياتهم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: الكناني
rows.claim: The poet’s line about the nāsiʾūn of Maʿadd and making months forbidden witnesses to the calendar intercalation practice.
rows.anchor: قال الكناني : ونحن الناسئون على معد

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Other commentators take the counters to be angels or people who remember the duration; al-Qurṭubī says to ask the calculators who know because the speakers forgot.
rows.anchor: والمفسرون جعلوا المراد من العادين الملائكة أو الناس الذين يتذكرون حساب مدة المكث

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority keep qāla in the past tense as continued reported dialogue; Ibn Kathīr, Ḥamzah, and al-Kisāʾī read the corresponding verb as an imperative.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { قال إن لبثتم إلا قليلا } قرأه الجمهور كما قرأوا الذي قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about years alerts them to their error: they had claimed that those buried in earth would never emerge.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام عن عدد سنوات المكث في الأرض مستعمل في التنبيه ليظهر لهم خطؤهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adad sinīn is a specification of the interrogative kam; sinīn is the actual specification, and adad reinforces the quantity already asked about.
rows.anchor: وانتصب { عدد سنين } على التمييز ل { كم } الاستفهامية والتمييز إنما هو { سنين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their answer shows they know they were underground but cannot recall the duration; they estimate a day or part of one by familiar earthly days, as in 30:55.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد بقولهم { يوما أو بعض يوم } أنهم قدروا مدة مكثهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question and answer indirectly prove they emerged alive from earth, refuting their denial and their claim that life cannot return to bones and remains after centuries.
rows.anchor: إيقافهم على ضلال اعتقادهم الماضي جيء به في قالب السؤال عن مدة مكثهم في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes them state that the stay seemed short to magnify their error: restored bodies and thought lead them to suppose little time passed, compounding their false premise.
rows.anchor: وقد ألجأهم الله إلى إظهار اعتقادهم قصر المدة التي بقوها زيادة في تشويه خطإهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their request to ask the counters admits they cannot measure the stay; they imagine the world still continues and disclaim responsibility for an imprecise answer.
rows.anchor: وأما قولهم : { فسئل العادين } فهو اعتراف بأنهم لم يضبطوا مدة مكثهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s answer requires an implied correction: they stayed for centuries, not a day; compared with God’s reckoning it was still little, as in 2:259 and 22:47.
rows.anchor: فكيف يجعل قليلا ، فتعين أن قوله : { إن لبثتم إلا قليلا } لا يستقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Law makes the knowledge counterfactual: they did not know the stay was little in God’s measure; it was long against their resurrection objection but short beside the torment ahead.
rows.anchor: وقرينة ذلك ما تفيده ( لو ) من الامتناع في قوله : { لو أنكم كنتم تعلمون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Weather signs follow the account of inspired guidance in animals: even inanimate matter follows its fixed divine course better than unbelievers with minds and senses, showing power, knowledge, and oneness.
rows.anchor: أعقب الدلالة على إعطاء الهدى في قوانين الإلهام في العجماوات بالدلالة على خلق الخصائص في الجماد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence of weather events is evidence for God’s power, wisdom, and knowledge, transitioning naturally to that argument.
rows.anchor: وقد حصل من هذا حسن التخلص للانتقال إلى الاستدلال على عظم القدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yuzjī means drives; God’s measured bringing of clouds together is likened to driving them until they become dense.
rows.anchor: و { يزجي } : يسوق . يقال : أزجى الإبل إزجاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joining the clouds is described as bringing their parts together; the cloud discussion is linked to 2:164 and 13:12.
rows.anchor: فانضمام بعض السحاب إلى بعض عبر عنه بالتأليف بين أجزائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayna takes a pronoun for cloud because clouds contain parts, as in Imruʾ al-Qays’s phrase between al-Dukhūl and Ḥawmal.
rows.anchor: ودخلت ( بين ) على ضمير السحاب لأن السحاب ذو أجزاء كقول امرىء القيس : بين الدخول فحومل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rukām derives from piling and means piled up; the pattern conveys a passive sense, as in 52:44.
rows.anchor: والركام : مشتق من الركم . والركم : الجمع والضم . ووزن فعال وفعالة يدل على معنى المفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some commentators identify the electrical discharge formed by stacked clouds as wadq; most say wadq is rain, the lexical-dictionary meaning, which exits through cloud gaps.
rows.anchor: فقال بعض المفسرين : هو الودق . وأكثر المفسرين على أن الودق هو المطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khilāl means openings or gaps, plural of khalal; 17:5 uses the same word.
rows.anchor: والخلال : الفتوق ، جمع خلل كجبل وجبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min al-samāʾ means falling from higher to lower, from the atmosphere to earth; here samāʾ means the sky above a given area of land.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { ينزل من السماء } يسقط من علو إلى سفل ، أي ينزل من جو السماء إلى الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min jibāl is a partitive apposition to al-samāʾ, with the mountains meaning cloud formations like mountains.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { من جبال } بدل من { السماء } بإعادة حرف الجر العامل في المبدل منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling something a mountain conveys great quantity; the Bukhārī report about a mountain of gold means the speaker would not want it to remain three nights, except money set aside for a debt.
rows.anchor: وإطلاق الجبال في تشبيه الكثرة معروف . يقال : فلان جبل علم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The min before jibāl and the first min are origin; the min in min barad is either extra in an affirmative sentence according to some grammarians or a noun meaning some.
rows.anchor: وحرف { من } الأول للابتداء و { من } الثاني كذلك و { من } في قوله { من برد } مزيدة في الإثبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of yunzilu is omitted but supplied by the phrase about hail inside the clouds: He sends down hail.
rows.anchor: ومفعول { ينزل } محذوف يدل عليه قوله : { فيها من برد } والتقدير : ينزل بردا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using min before barad also matches the preceding min jibāl.
rows.anchor: ووقوع { من } زائدة لقصد مشاكلة قوله : { من جبال }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling hail’s descent an ‘impact’ conveys harm, as muṣība means a painful occurrence; 9:50 shows ʾaṣāba can also indicate an ordinary event when context says good fortune.
rows.anchor: جعل نزول البرد إصابة لأن الإصابة إذا أطلقت في كلامهم دلت على أنها حلول مكروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root of aṣāba is ṣawb, descent, as in rain; hail is an impact because it damages crops, and the pronoun refers to hail.
rows.anchor: فجعل نزول البرد إصابة لأنه يفسد الزرع والثمرة ، فضمير { به } للبرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lightning description modifies the cloud and prompts reflection: people overlook familiar cloud formation, rain, and hail but remember lightning’s striking flashes as a sign of power.
rows.anchor: وفائدة هذه الصفة تنبيه العقول إلى التدبر في هذه التغيرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sana, without final hamza, means light of lightning or fire; sanāʾ with hamza means eminence, as shown by Ibn Durayd’s verse.
rows.anchor: والسنا مقصورا : ضوء البرق وضوء النار . وأما السناء الممدود فهو الرفعة

rows.speaker: ابن دريد
rows.claim: Ibn Durayd’s verse distinguishes the shortened and lengthened forms of sanā by contrasting light with honor.
rows.anchor: قال ابن دريد في أبيات له في متشابه المقصور والممدود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in al-abṣār denotes the class of eyes; the near-blinding lightning recalls 2:20, but this verse adds sanā because it focuses on cloud and rain as signs.
rows.anchor: ولام التعريف في { بالأبصار } لام الحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 2:20 the lightning belongs to a threatening portrait of hypocrites: rain seems beneficial but hides thunder, lightning, and calamities.
rows.anchor: وآية البقرة واردة في مقام التهديد والتشويه لحالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording in 24:43 says lightning almost removes eyesight, while 2:20 says it snatches eyesight; snatching conveys attack and domination beyond mere removal.
rows.anchor: ومن أجل اختلاف المقامين وضع التعبير هنا ب { يذهب بالأبصار } وهنالك بقوله : { يخطف أبصارهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite al-abṣār means the class of eyesight, as in 12:13 and the phrase enter the market; 2:20 instead specifies their eyes to rebuke them.
rows.anchor: وأما التعبير هنا ب { الأبصار } معرفا باللام فلأن المقصود أن البرق مقارب أن يزيل طائفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two versions vary a shared idea without needless repetition, preserving equal length and displaying the Qurʾān’s eloquence.
rows.anchor: وهكذا نرى بلاغة القرآن وإعجازه وحلاوة نظمه

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read yadhhab with open yāʾ and hāʾ; the bāʾ is causative, meaning it takes away eyesight.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { يذهب } بفتح التحتية وفتح الهاء ، فالباء للتعدية

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar alone reads yudhhib with a rounded yāʾ and kasra on hāʾ; the bāʾ is extra to emphasize attachment, as in 5:6.
rows.anchor: وقرأه أبو جعفر وحده بضم التحتية وكسر الهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transition from shadow and daylight to night and day is apt because night resembles shadow: darkness follows the sun’s light.
rows.anchor: مناسبة الانتقال من الاستدلال باعتبار أحوال الظل والضحاء إلى الاعتبار بأحوال الليل والنهار ظاهرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The defined parts of the clause indicate exclusive agency: only God makes night and day; Quraysh acknowledged His creation but their partners cannot share divine control, which cannot be divided.
rows.anchor: ومورد الاستدلال المقصد المستفاد من تعريف جزأي الجملة وهو قصر إفراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lakum attaches to jaʿala and names one benefit, not the only purpose; night results when the turning earth’s side is hidden from the sun and serves many ends, including 25:62.
rows.anchor: و { لكم } متعلق ب { جعل } أي من جملة ما خلق له الليل أنه يكون لباسا لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse shifts from first person to third person as an instance of iltifāt.
rows.anchor: وقد رجع أسلوب الكلام من المتكلم إلى الغيبة على طريقة الالتفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night is a direct metaphor as clothing that conceals people from one another, providing many benefits for private needs.
rows.anchor: و { لباسا } مشبه به على طريقة التشبيه البليغ ، أي ساترا لكم يستر بعضكم عن بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning night’s concealment before sleep suits the link between night and shadow; 78:8–10 orders sleep first because it matters more and connects more closely with creating spouses.
rows.anchor: وتقديم الاعتبار بحالة ستر الليل على الاعتبار بحالة النوم لرعي مناسبة الليل بالظل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse both argues and reminds: night-day alternation demonstrates the precise systems of earth’s rotation and sunlight, while night supports rest, renewed vigor, concealment, and day supports work and sight.
rows.anchor: وقد جمعت الآية استدلالا وامتنانا فهي دليل على عظم قدرة الخالق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect yadhdhakkar indicates repeated renewal of remembrance, while the verbal noun shukūr suggests gratitude can occur at once; arāda is repeated because the two forms do not coordinate smoothly.
rows.anchor: وجيء في جانب المتذكرين بقوله { أن يذكر } لدلالة المضارع على التجدد

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read yadhdhakkar with a doubled open dhāl, from yata-dhakkaru by assimilation of tāʾ into dhāl.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { أن يذكر } بتشديد الذال مفتوحة ، وأصله : يتذكر

rows.speaker: حمزة وخلف
rows.claim: Ḥamzah and Khalaf read yadhkur with a still dhāl and rounded kāf; it has the same meaning, though the doubled form implies greater effort, and both acts suit night and day.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة وخلف { أن يذكر } بسكون الذال وضم الكاف وهو بمعنى المشدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier peoples were stronger and longer-lived than Quraysh, received messengers, and were ultimately destroyed; Quraysh acknowledged these facts.
rows.anchor: كل أولئك كانوا أشد قوة من قريش وأكثر تعميرا في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that they were stronger explains the question about the end of earlier peoples; shidda literally means bodily firmness and metaphorically a quality hard to change, as in 27:33.
rows.anchor: وجملة { كانوا أشد منهم قوة } بيان لجملة { كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلهم .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quwwa is resistance to what would break something, extended from bodily or material strength to the capacities that repel harm and preserve sound conditions; a nation’s strength includes military resources, wealth, children, and spouses.
rows.anchor: والقوة : حالة بها يقاوم صاحبها ما يوجب انخرامه ، فمن ذلك قوة البدن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh could not approach those peoples’ strength; ʿĀd were proverbial for might, so Arabs call anything great in its kind ʿādī.
rows.anchor: وحالة مشركي قريش لا تداني أحوال تلك الأمم في القوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Athārū is coordinated with kānū and derives from stirring or turning something settled; 30:48 also uses athāra for winds moving clouds.
rows.anchor: وعطف { أثاروا } على { كانوا } فهو فعل مشتق من الإثارة بكسر الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Athārū can mean tilling, turning buried soil outward, as in 2:71; al-Nābigha’s line about wild cattle turning gravel witnesses this sense.
rows.anchor: وأطلقت الإثارة هنا على قلب تراب الأرض بجعل ما كان باطنا ظاهرا وهو الحرث

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nābigha’s verse describes wild cattle turning gravel until they reach its coolness, evidencing athāra as turning up soil.
rows.anchor: وقال النابغة يصف بقر الوحش إذا حفرت التراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: More apt to the point about strength is a figurative sense: these peoples exercised sweeping power over the land and its inhabitants, like stirring something still; the word thawra derives similarly.
rows.anchor: وهذا الاحتمال أنسب بالمقصود الذي هو وصف الأمم بالقوة والمقدرة
